preamble: Spirantization of the aspirated bilabial stop [pʰ] to the labiodental fricative [f]. Classical Attic φ was an aspirated stop [pʰ]; during the Koine and Byzantine periods it became a fricative, giving Modern Greek [f] in φίλος, φόβος, φωνή and φως. Wiktionary transcribes 4th-century Koine φ as bilabial [ɸ] and 10th-century Byzantine φ as [f]; that bilabial stage is a reconstructed pronunciation, not distinguished in spelling.
